correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the all-integer n>=3 result for the Euclidean unit-edge uniform n-antiprism, with a=pi/(2n), H=sqrt(4cos(a)^2-1), and three unoriented line directions (cos(2pi j/3),sin(2pi j/3),H). Unit-edge geometry gives R=1/(2sin(2a)), h=H/(2cos a), and four outward facet normals e3, (gamma,0,-zeta), (gamma cos(2a), +/- gamma sin(2a),zeta), where gamma=H/(sqrt(3)cos a), zeta=tan(a)/sqrt(3). Verified gamma^2+zeta^2=1 and zeta H=gamma sin a. Their four strict scalar products reduce X-raying each upper vertex of angle theta to circular distance(theta,phi)<beta=pi/2-a; by bottom-face reflection/rotation, the lower criterion is circular distance(theta-pi,phi)<beta. For n>3, beta>pi/3 and 3 arcs of centers 0,2pi/3,4pi/3 cover every angle; for n=3 the only uncovered angles are arc midpoints, while all transformed upper/lower vertex angles are arc centers. Inclusion of each face Gauss image in an incident vertex Gauss image covers the full boundary; the universal d-dimensional X-ray lower bound gives X>=3. Verified failure of the almost-smooth condition because e3 dot m0=-tan(a)/sqrt(3)<0<1/2. Independently regenerated convex hull facets of both vertex rings and numerically tested all incident outward normals and strict direction signs for every integer 3<=n<=120 (without relying on packaged verify.py), maximum unit-normal mismatch 1.30e-15 and smallest computed best-direction strict dot 0.1139. This finite diagnostic does not establish the quantified theorem; the exact trigonometric proof does.
residual_risks: Floating-point finite regression covers only 3<=n<=120; the analytic normal-cone and circular covering argument supplies the infinite conclusion.
The claim is restricted to convex uniform metric antiprisms, not arbitrary combinatorial realizations.

value.rationale: Uniform antiprisms form a canonical infinite family of convex uniform three-polytopes, making their exact X-ray number a natural geometric invariant. The n=3 regular octahedron case is already known, but the theorem resolves every n>=4 simultaneously, including an explicit dimension-minimal three-direction certificate with unchanged 120-degree azimuths and a natural n-dependent common slope. The proof connects vertex normal cones to exact circular arcs and shows the family is outside the only close broad sufficient class of almost-smooth bodies. This is a mathematically motivated family-level classification rather than a named-object substitution or a finite catalog.
residual_risks: The result does not determine X-ray numbers of nonuniform antiprism realizations, nor ordinary illumination numbers.
No claim of a general classification of all convex polyhedra is made.
